vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pmbuysell
Version: 1.0.2

The pmbuysell skill bundle is a legitimate Polymarket trading tool designed for AI agents. It provides a structured interface for managing accounts, checking balances, and executing trades via the official Polymarket CLOB API. While the skill handles sensitive data such as private keys and API credentials (stored in a local .env file and a data/ cache directory), its behavior is strictly aligned with its stated purpose. The code interacts only with legitimate Polymarket endpoints (clob.polymarket.com and gamma-api.polymarket.com) and lacks any indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection. A 'Pro' feature for auto-redemption is mentioned as a paid addon via a Telegram contact (@taroers), which serves as a simple monetization paywall rather than a security threat.

llm.summary: The package appears to implement the described Polymarket trading functionality, but registry metadata omits required environment variables/dependencies and the code will read/write local .env and cache files (including private keys), so there are inconsistencies you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code implements Polymarket trading and balance queries (uses private keys, funder addresses, py_clob_client, requests, dotenv)—which matches the skill's stated purpose. However the registry metadata declares no required env vars or binaries while the implementation clearly requires .env variables (PM_ACCOUNT_IDS, ACCx_PRIVATE_KEY, ACCx_FUNDER) and Python dependencies (dotenv, py_clob_client, requests). This mismatch between declared requirements and actual needs is a coherence concern.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits actions to creating/validating a .env, installing pip deps, and running CLI functions. The code does not call unexpected external endpoints beyond Polymarket/CLoB APIs (e.g., gamma-api.polymarket.com and configurable CLOB_HOST). One scope note: local_config loads both pmbuysell/.env and a parent project .env (fallback), so if you run from a project root the skill may read unrelated environment variables present there.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no marketplace install spec (no automated download). SKILL.md instructs manual pip install -r pmbuysell/requirements.txt; code depends on third‑party packages (python-dotenv, requests, py_clob_client). Lack of an explicit install entry in registry combined with non-trivial external dependencies is a packaging/visibility issue (not inherently malicious but worth attention).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs private keys and funder addresses to trade, so requesting ACCx_PRIVATE_KEY and ACCx_FUNDER is proportionate to its purpose. The concern is that these required env vars are not declared in the registry metadata, and local_config will load a project-level .env as a fallback—potentially exposing other unrelated secrets if present. The code also caches derived API creds to disk (pmbuysell/data), so secrets/creds are persisted locally unencrypted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not request elevated platform privileges. It does create and write local files (.env template, cache files under pmbuysell/data), which is expected for this functionality. It does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be what it says (Polymarket trading), but pay attention to these points before installing: 1) It requires private keys and funder addresses stored in .env (PM_ACCOUNT_IDS + ACCx_PRIVATE_KEY/ACCx_FUNDER). The registry metadata did not declare those — verify where you will store keys. 2) local_config will also load a parent project .env if present; avoid running this from a directory that contains unrelated secrets. 3) The code caches derived API credentials to disk (pmbuysell/data) unencrypted — treat that directory as sensitive. 4) Dependencies (python-dotenv, requests, py_clob_client) must be installed; review their provenance and the package's requirements.txt. 5) If you intend the agent to autonomously invoke this skill, be cautious: trading operations use real private keys and can move funds. Recommended actions: run in an isolated environment, use limited-scope or testnet keys if possible, inspect pmbuysell/requirements.txt and the code yourself, and ensure your .env contains only the minimal keys you intend to expose.
